items.name: block-typography
items.title: Slide typography
items.description: Two primitives every other block builds on. Eyebrow is an uppercase accent label at --slide-label-size with --slide-label-tracking letter spacing, in --primary. SlideHeading is an h1 at --slide-heading-size capped at 1500 canvas pixels with an optional lead paragraph at --slide-lead-size in --muted-foreground capped at 1100. The measures are canvas pixels rather than a ch count because the canvas is 1920 wide and never changes, so where a title breaks is a fixed decision instead of one that moves with the heading face. Both read the theme's size tokens rather than Tailwind text sizes, so they resize when you retune the type scale, and both name their parts: data-slide-eyebrow, data-slide-title, and data-slide-lead. Add this if you are writing your own slide layouts and want the deck's heading rhythm without copying class strings. Every other Deckard block depends on it.

items.name: block-slide-layouts
items.title: Slide layouts
items.description: The five whole-slide frames a deck reaches for most. HeroSlide runs the height of the frame with the eyebrow on the top edge and the title block on the bottom one, at --slide-title-size, and takes an optional meta array for the credit row every source template's opener carries. BreakerSlide is the same rhythm centered vertically, for a section divider, and takes an optional index string that themes set oversized above the title. Both are left aligned, like the frame. ContentSlideCard puts an eyebrow, heading, and lead above a bordered --slide-surface panel, and is for body content with no surface of its own. OpenContentSlide is the same intro with no panel, for content that brings its own frame: a FeatureGrid, a BulletList, a chart. FocusSlide is the slide that is one block and nothing else, a code sample or a list or an image with no heading around it: it hands the block the whole frame at the normal type scale, so a code sample shows more lines rather than bigger ones, and takes one optional kicker string. All five pull the title from useSlideTitle() when you do not pass one, so a slide's title stays defined in one place. They respect --slide-content-gap, --slide-item-gap, --slide-radius-lg, --slide-surface, --slide-surface-border, and --slide-surface-shadow, and they name their parts with data-slide-hero, data-slide-hero-meta, data-slide-breaker, data-slide-breaker-index, data-slide-intro, data-slide-panel, and data-slide-kicker, which is how a theme swap restyles them with no edits.

items.name: block-collections
items.title: Slide collections
items.description: Two ways to put a list on a slide without it turning into a wall of bullets. BulletList numbers each item 01, 02, 03 in a left rail and rules the rows off with a bottom border, at --slide-body-size on a 62ch measure, so the line length holds when a FocusSlide swaps the body size up. FeatureGrid lays three cards across on --slide-surface-muted, each with a title at --slide-subheading-size and a supporting paragraph at --slide-support-size. Both name their parts, data-slide-list through data-slide-list-text and data-slide-grid through data-slide-card-body, which is how phosphor writes a [x] where the number goes and ledger hangs a rule there instead. Both carry data-slide-surface, which is what makes a ContentSlideCard around them warn rather than quietly frame a frame; compose them through OpenContentSlide or FocusSlide instead. Both are presentational and take plain arrays, so a server component can await the data and pass it straight in. Use BulletList for four to six sequential points and FeatureGrid for three parallel ones. Neither scrolls, so trim the copy instead of adding a seventh item.

items.name: block-media
items.title: Slide media
items.description: Photo and video slides that fill the 1920x1080 canvas properly. FullscreenMediaSlide bleeds an image or a video to every edge and lays optional copy over the bottom on one of three scrims, from --slide-media-overlay-subtle to -strong; the framed variant insets it in a bordered surface instead. ImageShowcaseSlide splits the canvas 1.2fr to 0.8fr, image left and a caption panel right. Both take next/image sources, forward blurDataURL from a static import when the source carries one, take unoptimized so an SVG served from public/ skips the image optimizer instead of needing dangerouslyAllowSVG, and use SlideMediaVideo from @deckard/core so video pauses on slides the audience is not looking at. Both pad against --slide-chrome-top and --slide-chrome-bottom, so the deck header and slide counter never sit on top of a caption, and both name their parts: data-slide-media, data-slide-media-overlay, data-slide-media-caption, and data-slide-media-credit. Use these instead of dropping an img on a slide, which will not fit the canvas and will not respect the chrome.

items.name: block-metrics
items.title: Slide metrics
items.description: One export, StatGrid, for the figures slide every deck reaches for once. It takes two, three, or four stats, typed as a union of tuples so a fifth is a compile error and a lone figure is too, and marks them up as a description list that splits into as many equal columns as it was given. Each column is a figure at --slide-figure-size in --slide-font-heading, an optional unit suffix at --slide-figure-unit-size, an optional meter bar at --slide-meter-size showing a rough proportion between 0 and 1, a caption at --slide-support-size capped to 26 characters a line, and a 2px rule across the top in --slide-surface-border. It sets no color of its own, so the rule picks up the theme border weight, and it carries data-slide-surface so a panel around it says it is framing a frame. In a FocusSlide three numbers carry the whole canvas with nothing else around them. Every part of a column is named for themes to reach: data-stat-grid, data-stat-item, data-stat-value, data-stat-unit, data-stat-meter, and data-stat-caption. Take the caption seriously. A number on a slide without the thing it is measured against is decoration, and the 26ch measure is sized for "up from 2.6k", not for a sentence. The meter is a proportion, not a chart: if you cannot say what it is a proportion of, leave it out.

items.name: preset-blocks
items.title: Deckard blocks
items.description: Every slide block in one add, plus the one stylesheet line a consumer cannot guess: the @import of @deckard/core/styles.css, which carries the slide token contract and registers the package's own Tailwind source so the runtime classes survive tree shaking. Use this once, right after installing @deckard/core, then write slides. The theme is not in here and does not need to be: the six Deckard themes are named exports of @deckard/themes, so a deck picks one with an import rather than an install.
items.docs: The blocks land in app/slides/blocks/, and the stylesheet import above is the whole build wiring. @deckard/core ships compiled and its stylesheet registers its own Tailwind source, so there is no transpilePackages entry and no @source line for you to add. What is left is deck code: create deck/deck.ts, import a theme from @deckard/themes, pass it to defineDeck, then render the deck from app/slides/[id]/page.tsx with createSlideRoute from @deckard/core/next. Run deckard eject theme when you want that theme as three files in deck/theme/ you can edit.
